text: What's the matter? Did you kill him? No, of course not. He was dead. Dead? They're just on the point of attacking us. Grandfather, what are they going to do? Well, continue with our plan. Get the keys and get out of here as soon as possible. What I do now is warn Marco. Be careful, Ian. Wake the bearers. What is it? Bandits. What's he doing for you? Never mind about that. The guard's been killed. Now wake the bearers and get some sauce. Quickly, call the others. Doctor, Susan, Barbara. Quickly, here. That's right, Susan. Go.
Go into the tent and save her. What about Team Chess? She sleeps now, but if she wakes up, make sure she stays with you.
Are the bearers awake? Yes, sir. They're taking their positions around the edge of a creek.
Do you know how to use one of these? No, but given half a chance, I'll learn.
Pardon me. If you're half as aggressive with this as you are with your tongue, Doctor, we can't lose.
How many of them are there likely to be?
We look a bit silly standing here, don't we? What do you suggest we do?
Do TARDIS. Caravan to go where? Yes, get out of here. Anywhere where it's safe.
Where it's safe? Look, this is another of the magician's tricks.
I don't believe there are any bandits. Sagana, a guard is dead.
Well, could they have not killed him? What better way to give this lie the ring of truth?
Not everyone lives by your standards, Sagana. Well, where are these bandits, if there are any?
Why haven't they attacked? I warn you, Marco, if you go in their caravan, it will surely destroy you.
If you believe that, Toto, you're a bigger fool than even I think you are.
You've deceived me before, Doctor.
No, we will not use your caravan. If there are bandits, we shall fight them.
Well, we're not going to get very far with this overgrown bread knife. We shall have to use more enterprise than this.
The dox is right, Marco. We need more than these swords, so we can outwit them.
How?
We'll use this bamboo.
We'll work up with that, too.
If we throw it on the fire, it will expand and blow up. It's a terrifying noise. It's worth a chance, Marco.
Let us hope time is our ally. The moon will soon rise to deny us darkness.
Perhaps he is sleeping.
He is not as young. Tell the others that unless he signals before the moon's first light...
Yes, my lord, come on.
But we'll still... we'll make sport of it.
Does the lamb consume the wolf, or the wolf the lamb?
Were you trying to escape?
Yes.
It was very reckless of him.
It was the only thing we could do.
Even though failure might have meant death?
We hoped we'd succeed.
Tony, what were you going to do for me?
Take the key.
Take the key from you?
And use you as a hostage until we were safely at the TARDIS.
Then I shall have to be more careful in future.
I wish I could explain to you how important the TARDIS is to us.
And I wish I could explain to you, Ian, how important it is to me.
The moon will soon be up.
Yes. We must gamble if the attack comes now.
We can't wait for that.
They are alert, Marco.
There are three of them.
They may wake their doctor.
Bamboo will need time to heat up.
Yes, we must gamble if the attack comes now.
There are no bandits.
This was all a ruse.
A ruse, Stegun.
Good luck, Ian.
Wake up, Ian.
The bandits thought there were devils in the fire and fled.
No.
It wasn't the devils in the fire.
Their leader is killed.
That's why they broke up and ran.
Well, in battle all men face death.
And few expect to meet it.
At sunrise, we buried the dead.
And we buried the dead.
Broke camp.
Traveled to the edge of the bamboo forest.
And out beyond it, onto the plain.
But at midday, as we were all tired after the events of the previous night, I ordered a halt.
Surely he can't punish us.
By trying to escape, we saved his life.
If we had any decency at all, he'd let us go.
I doubt he'll do that, Doctor.
Well, then we must go on trying to escape.
Circuit's finished and all we need are those keys.
That's not going to be very easy, is it, after last night?
Marco's bound to be on his guard.
I have a question to ask all of you.
Will you promise on your honor not to attempt another escape?
So be it.
We sacrificed our freedom to save you.
Yes, I know.
And in return, I revoke the seizure of your caravan by official decree.
Very noble of you, I'm sure.
What you're really saying, Marco, is that we're no longer Kublai Khan's prisoners.
Only yours, eh?
That's right.
Thanks for nothing.
All the freedoms you enjoyed before will be restored.
Susan and Ping Cho can share each other's company.
And no guards will watch you by night.
And the keys to the TARDIS?
As before, Doctor.
They remain with me.
And I shall be guarded day and night.
Marco, let me be your sword.
You are in my charge, Sagana, not I am yours.
Put your magic on him if you will.
Make no move against me.
He knows we're not to him.
Strange that Sagana should watch the fire.
The sort of menial job he'd order a guard to do.
How could he? The guard was dead.
Sagana wasn't to know that. Otherwise he'd have given the alarm.
Would he?
You mean he was implicated in the attack?
Of course he was.
The bandit knew him. I'm certain he did.
Ian, do you remember that bandit we buried this morning?
I knew I'd seen him somewhere before.
He was in the cave of 500 eyes.
Yes, and he had to kill him or be exposed.
What's Sagana's game? What's he after?
My ship.
Oh, no, Doctor. He's terrified of it.
Must be something else.
Whatever it is, we're in the way. That's for sure.
Marco too?
I don't know. Maybe.
Well, shouldn't we warn him?
No, no, shush. We mustn't be impetuous.
But choose the right moment. Carefully.
It's a courier from Kuplai Khan. Have you seen Mr. Marco?
Yes, he's in there.
Please be seated.
Thank you, my lady.
I will fetch him. His name is Ling Tao.
You look as though you've travelled far.
From the Summer Palace at Shang Tu, my lord.
What is it, Ping Chou?
A courier from the Great Khan has arrived, Mr. Marco.
Ask him to wait, please. I'll be with him in a moment.
Ping Chou, do I have your word not to tell anyone where these keys are?
Yes, Mr. Marco.
When did you leave Shang Tu?
Yesterday, my lord.
Yesterday?
What?
That's 300 miles away, isn't it?
We change horses every league, my lord.
Every league?
That's the reason we wear these, my lord.
To warn the post house of our arrival.
When we get there, our fresh horse is saddled and waiting, ready for the next three miles.
And you ride without rest until you reach your destination?
Yes, my lady.
I would have thought it was a physical impossibility.
Our bodies would be shaken to pieces, my lord.
Were it not for these, bound tight like this one on my head.
Tell me, are there many men who can ride such long distances without a break?
We are few, my lord.
300 miles a day on horseback.
Very few people can ride more than 25.
It's in our blood, my lord.
We all come from the great steppes to the north.
Courier.
My lord Polo.
I am he.
The mighty Kubla Khan sends his greetings to his faithful servant.
Thank you.
Thank you.
We must leave here at once.
Why, Mr. Marco?
Kubla Khan wishes to see me without delay.
Six days' hard riding from here is the city of Cheng Ting, where we can take horses and ride on to Shang Tu.
But our positions, Mr. Marco?
They will have to follow on one of the many trade caravans that travels the route.
And the TARDIS?
That too must follow on, doctor.
My only concern now is to reach the Summer Palace as quickly as possible.
So, within an hour, we were on the move again.
And on the sixth day of our journey, the spires of Cheng Ting will be seen on our horizon.
By later afternoon, we had arrived at the way station of the White City, as Cheng Ting is often called.
And how long will you honor us with your presence, my lord?
We have to ride to Shang Tu tomorrow.
Oh, how sad.
Good day, my gracious ladies.
Cheng Ting is so delightful at this time of the year.
Well?
Where is it?
What?
The TARDIS.
Dear, dear, dear.
Pending arrival, my lord Marco, by a courier who passed this way from Cheng Ting.
What is it now?
I thought you said the TARDIS was to be placed in the courtyard.
To what does the old lord refer?
His caravan.
Oh, that's what it is.
I had it moved.
Where to?
The stables, my lord.
The stables.
Well, I could hardly leave it in a hanging garden, my lord.
Now, could I?
It'll be safe enough there, doctor.
What...
When does the next commerce caravan leave for Cheng Ting?
The day after tomorrow, my lord.
Well, you see that all baggage goes with it, including that caravan.
I shall make it a personal duty, my lord Marco.
And now, if you step this way, I'll escort you to your apartment.
I could hardly have it placed in the hanging garden, now could I?
What does he think it is, a potting shed or something?
Well, it's better there than in the courtyard, doctor.
At least it's out of sight.
Look at that one there.
He's just like Wang Lo.
All fat, smooth and smooth.
Look at this one here.
He's very solemn.
He's just like Marco Polo.
Look at this one bashing around all over the place.
He's got Ian's energy.
Ah, look.
That one's all by itself.
It's independent, like Barclay.
There's you, Susan.
Hm?
A wicked goldfish.
Now, where are you being chilled?
Oh, look there.
That little pretty one down there with the wedding veil.
Shh.
Oh, wait.
Oh, look.
Oh, look.
I'm sorry.
How I miss my home in Samarkand.
And your home, Susan, has never told me about that.
It is so very far away.
Yes it is.
It's as far away as a night star.
But you can reach it from Venice, can't you?
No, Bing Jo.
No, I can't.
And if Messer Marco does give your caravan to Kublai Khan's, you will never see your
home again.
That's right.
I gave him my word, Susan.
I gave him my word, Susan.
I promise not to tell anyone where he put the key.
And I promise you that no one will ask you.
What is it, Lord?
A warlord's tomb.
I want it.
Can you arrange to have it taken for me?
You prepare to pay a good price?
How much?
We want gold, not Kublai Khan's paper money.
You shall have it.
In advance.
One half tonight.
The other half when I get the tomb.
A hundred golden pieces.
You shall have it.
That first part, my lord.
When do I receive it?
Tonight.
The street of the Beggars at midnight.
I shall be there.
So shall I.
A warlord's tomb.
More than that.
A Khan's throne for no guy.
Come in.
It is dinner time, Mr. Markov.
Thank you, Pinktoe.
Oh, dear.
I have ink on my fingers.
I will join you there.
Something to give you.
What is it?
Can't you guess?
This.
Miss Messer Markov.
Not to tell anyone.
I haven't.
You don't know where I got it.
Terribly angry.
But one of us will be on the way home.
Good night, ladies.
Good night, my lord.
No, I don't think so.
Let me go up to our room before you tell the others.
Yes, all right.
You will say good night.
You will say goodbye, won't you?
Of course I will.
Pinktoe, what can I say?
Haven't you any ideas?
Why don't you have a drink?
Close the doors.
Must have gone to say goodbye to Pinktoe.
What on earth is that child doing?
I think she's doing great omnipresence.
Don't panic.
Give her a second.
I knocked out the guard.
